principle_text: When the persuadee expresses curiosity about your role and motivation, avoid giving vague or off-topic responses that do not clarify your purpose or engage their interest.
When the persuadee expresses unfamiliarity with the activity, avoid emphasizing your own inexperience as it may reduce their confidence in the interaction.
When the persuadee is already actively volunteering time and services, avoid focusing solely on encouraging monetary donations without acknowledging their existing contributions.
When the persuadee shares their volunteer involvement but not monetary donations, avoid simply expressing similarity without advancing the conversation toward donation opportunities.
When the persuadee expresses concern about how donations are used, avoid vague or generalized statements about money allocation without providing transparent and specific information.
When the persuadee expresses concern about the misuse of donations and demands transparency, avoid vague assurances and instead provide clear, verifiable information about how funds are used.
When the persuadee expresses uncertainty about the task and focuses on honesty, avoid only clarifying roles without introducing persuasive content related to the charity or donation.
